Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/9] Power to detect significance in the slopes for SWL was noticeably lower, ranging from .55 and .66 (for wives and husbands, respectively) at the lowest sample size, up to .79 and .87 at the largest sample size. Power ranged from .62 to .83 to detect change in satisfaction with life using the common fate growth model. While there are noticeable differences in power for the CSI and SWLS, there does not appear to be a difference in power for the Common Fate and correlated growth models. The difference in power to detect change in the SWLS and CSI point to the difficulty in recommending particular sample sizes when comparing these two models.
